text:
Alex: Quick question — I'm capturing with nsys to dig into kernel selection + batching heuristics + KV cache hotspots. What CLI flags are we standardizing on for a focused trace (need cuda kernels, nvtx regions, OSRT timers) without ending up with multi-GB files?

Sam: For those three traces use nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt. Limit the time window with capture-range or capture-duration to avoid huge files. Keep sampling conservative.

Priya: Here's a compact command I use for a representative request window (annotate the code paths with NVTX around batching/KV ops):
```bash
nsys profile -o out/kv_batch_hotspot \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --sample=timer --sample-freq=1000 \
  --capture-range=nvtx:prof_begin:prof_end \
  --capture-duration=45s \
  --stats=true \
  --force-overwrite \
  -- python -u run_infer.py --model=serve/latest --workload=batch_stream
```
Notes: put nvtx pushes around request start/end, batching decisions, KV cache get/evict. capture-range helps capture only the interesting part.

Sam: If you want lower disk use --sample=none and rely on OSRT+NVTX timings for wall-clock and kernel order; sampling is only needed if you want host-side CPU sampling heatmaps.

Alex: Any heuristics for sample-freq / duration? Last time we filled disk quickly when testing long tail.

Priya: For short repros 20-60s with sample-freq 1000 is okay (~200-400MB typical depending on kernel density). For long runs do repeated short captures per scenario or drop sample to none. Also exclude other noisy processes on the GPU.

perf-bot: Note: profile output files: out/kv_batch_hotspot.qdrep and out/kv_batch_hotspot.sqlite (qdrep is what we open in UI).

Sam: When inspecting kernel-selection problems watch for: many small kernel launches interleaved with memcpy, or long idle gaps that indicate kernel fallback. Group by symbol+module in the timeline and sort by duration to find hotspots.

Alex: Any quick NVTX annotation patterns you recommend for KV cache ops?

Priya: Mark enter/exit for: batch_assemble, kernel_select, kv_lookup_hit, kv_lookup_miss, kv_evict, kv_prefetch. Example in python: nvtx.range_push("kv_lookup_miss") / nvtx.range_pop(). That makes it trivial to filter traces to just the miss window.

Sam: Also export callstacks if you need deeper host-side attribution: add --export=callstacks or enable callstack capture in options (adds size but useful). And add --stats=true for post-run aggregate summaries.

Alex: What about CUDA context switches / preemption noise? We saw weird gaps last week.

Sam: Check OSRT lanes and kernel concurrency in the timeline. If you see frequent context switches, correlate with other processes on the GPU or with our preemption thresholds. In some cases pinning the workload to specific devices (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES) during trace helps reduce noise.

Priya: For KV eviction chasing: look for repeated small memcpy + kernel sequences at the same NVTX region timestamp; that typically means the cache path is doing extra copies on miss.

Sam: Final housekeeping: commit the exact nsys command, GPU driver, CUDA, cupti versions, and runtime flags to the trace artifact so later comparisons are meaningful (we put a small text file next to the qdrep).

Alex: Great, I'll run the 45s capture with NVTX markers around batch + kv and share the qdrep here. Thanks!
